title: Design for responsible AI and human oversight
summary: Users need to know when AI is involved, how far to trust it and how to correct it. Design for mistakes, fairness and human oversight from the start.

beginner: Tell users clearly when they are dealing with AI.
Show how confident the AI is, or why it gave an answer, where that helps.
Let users correct, override or report wrong answers.
Decide where a human must check before anything important happens.
Test with a range of users to spot unfair results.
Plan what the product does when the AI fails or is unavailable.
intermediate: Design transparency, control and feedback into the experience.
Define human review points by risk.
experienced: Run a structured risk assessment using a recognised framework.
Set red lines for uses you will not support.
Build governance with legal, security and ethics colleagues.

canDelegateTo.task: Test for bias and failure modes

toolExamples.figma: Design error, low-confidence and fallback states, not just the happy path.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep an AI risk register linked to design decisions.

definitionOfDone: AI use is clear to users
pitfalls: No human check on high-impact decisions
